newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB, CWC in talks on pay-per-view - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB, CWC in talks on pay-per-view - newspaper.

text.p: British satellite television operator BSkyB and telecommunications firm Cable and Wireless Communications are in talks over cooperation on pay-per-view television, due to be launched next year, according to a report in the Sunday Telegraph newspaper.

A Cable and Wireless spokeswoman said the company would not comment on speculation, while BSkyB was not immediately available for comment. The two companies are competing with each other to launch digital services some time next year.
The newspaper said that if successful, the talks could mean that Cable and Wireless would use BSkyB programming and administration to run its pay-per-view business.
The Sunday Telegraph said Cable and Wireless might contracting out all its television operations to BSkyB in the longer term.
Pay-per-view television would allow customers to select and pay for individual programmes watched. BSkyB has already used pay-per-view for some key sporting events.
Cable and Wireless and BSkyB are competing with each other to set up digital services, with BSkyB targeting a launch of 200-channel digital satellite services in spring 1998 in Britain.
Cable and Wireless Chief Executive Graham Wallace said earlier this month that the company could start digital services before BSkyB but might wait to launch at the same time.
